title: Benchmark window guardrails: canary gating + auto-abort/rollback plan to protect production SLOs
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description: Summary: Adds benchmark-window guardrails to perf-canary so benchmark-lab region runs cannot silently degrade production SLOs. This PR introduces (1) a canary gate that validates region health and a small control workload before permitting the full benchmark suite, (2) continuous SLO monitors during the window with automatic abort criteria, and (3) a documented rollback/abort plan with clear on-call ownership + artifacts. Motivation: Benchmark runs for the latency/$ report are intentionally load-heavy (high concurrency, sustained duration). Even when scheduled into capacity windows, we need hard stops if they push shared infra into unsafe territory (p95 latency, error rate, GPU saturation). This is specifically to reduce the risk that benchmark execution regresses production routing tiers and to make our external methodology credible (“we measured without impacting customer traffic”). Scope: This PR only adds guardrails and automation around benchmark windows. It does NOT change benchmark methodology parameters (concurrency, prompts, caching/batching flags) and does NOT change production autoscaling policies. Design overview: The guardrails are implemented as a thin controller around existing perf-canary hooks. Before a benchmark window begins, we run a 3–5 minute “preflight canary” against the target region (control model set + control prompt distribution) and validate against baseline thresholds. If preflight fails, the window is blocked and we page the benchmark on-call + SRE on-call with a summary. During the benchmark window, we stream region metrics (p95 end-to-end latency, 5xx rate, queue depth, GPU utilization, admission control rejects) and enforce abort triggers. Abort triggers are conservative and biased toward protecting production; they include both absolute thresholds and delta-from-baseline thresholds to avoid punishing naturally slower regions. On abort, the runner (a) terminates active benchmark jobs, (b) applies a “benchmark traffic deny” policy tag to prevent immediate retries, (c) posts a Slack incident-style summary (without creating a formal incident) including links to dashboards and the run artifacts, and (d) writes an auditable marker in the run manifest. Rollback plan: If abort triggers fire or SRE determines production risk, immediate action is to stop benchmark traffic. If the benchmark runner changed any routing headers or quota overrides (it shouldn’t, but this handles edge cases), the rollback script resets the benchmark service account quotas and removes region override headers from the runner config. We also provide a manual kill-switch in case the controller is unhealthy. Ownership/Runbook: Adds a short runbook section: who is paged, how to acknowledge, how to re-run preflight, and what evidence is required to resume (2 clean preflights + region health green for 15 minutes). Implementation details: - New guardrails config with per-region defaults and ability to override via env for emergency runs. - Preflight canary job uses the same client stack as benchmark-lab but is capped at low QPS and uses a fixed seed for prompt selection. - Baseline is computed as median of the last 5 “healthy” preflights in that region (stored in the perf-canary artifact bucket), with a fallback static baseline if history is empty. - Abort triggers: (a) p95 latency > 1.25x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-min windows OR absolute p95 > 2.5s for chat routes, (b) 5xx rate > 0.6% for 2 consecutive windows, (c) admission rejects > 2% for 2 consecutive windows, (d) GPU utilization > 92% AND queue depth increasing for 5 minutes (proxy for saturation), (e) SRE manual abort via Slack command. - All thresholds are deliberately conservative and intended to be revisited after the first two full benchmark cycles. Changed areas/files (high-level): - controller/benchmark_window_controller.py: orchestrates preflight -> full run -> monitoring -> abort. - monitors/slo_watchdog.py: streaming evaluation + hysteresis logic. - rollback/abort_benchmark_window.sh: kill-switch and quota reset. - config/guardrails.defaults.yaml: threshold defaults. - docs/runbooks/benchmark-window-guardrails.md: on-call instructions and evidence checklist. - integrations/slack_notifier.py: summary formatting + linking to dashboards/artifacts. - tests/test_slo_watchdog.py + tests/test_preflight_gate.py: unit tests for thresholds and failure modes. Example snippet (abort summary): "ABORTED benchmark window us-east-1: p95 latency 1.34x baseline for 3m (baseline=780ms, current=1045ms). 5xx=0.2% (ok). GPU=94% with rising queue depth. Action taken: runner stopped, benchmark deny tag applied. Next steps: wait 15m, re-run preflight x2; if still failing, escalate to SRE." Testing: - Unit tests for hysteresis/threshold math + baseline fallback behavior. - Local dry-run using recorded metrics stream fixtures. - Staging run in eu-west-1 with forced-threshold toggles to validate abort/rollback behavior. Notes/risks: - False positives: We may abort in legitimately noisy windows; that is acceptable for this project since the cost of production impact is much higher than the cost of rerunning benchmarks. - Baseline drift: Using last-5 healthy preflights should track drift reasonably; we also log baseline versioning in the run manifest so methodology reviewers can see what baseline was used. - Metric gaps: If a required metric stream is missing for >90 seconds, we fail closed and abort (protect prod). Follow-ups: - Hook guardrail abort markers into the benchmark anomaly triage playbook so rerun policy is explicit. - After first report cycle, revisit thresholds with Perf/Evals + SRE and adjust per region/model family if needed.
commits: feat(controller): add preflight canary gate for benchmark windows
feat(monitors): implement SLO watchdog with hysteresis + baseline comparison
feat(rollback): add abort script + deny-tag application
docs(runbook): benchmark window guardrails + evidence checklist
test: add fixtures + unit tests for watchdog and preflight gate
chore: wire slack notifier summary + artifact links
review_conversation: Neha Kapoor (request changes): Thresholds look reasonable, but the GPU saturation trigger seems too brittle. Can we add the queue-depth rising condition so we don’t abort on transient spikes? Also, fail-closed on metric gaps is OK, but please make the Slack message explicit about the reason. Keiko Yamamoto (author): Good call. I updated the GPU trigger to require >92% utilization AND rising queue depth for 5 minutes; also added explicit Slack messaging and a run-manifest marker when we abort due to metric gaps. Sean Gallagher (approve): Preflight gate is the right approach. One concern: baseline fallback is static—do we log when we’re using fallback so we can interpret aborts? Keiko Yamamoto: Yes, now logs baseline_source=(history|fallback) and includes baseline_version in the manifest. Peter Holtz (request changes): Abort script should also clear any residual benchmark headers/quota overrides even if the runner failed mid-run. Add idempotency and a “dry-run” mode for on-call confidence. Keiko Yamamoto: Added idempotent checks + --dry-run output. Claire Dubois (approve): From methodology perspective, this is strong and aligns with our “don’t impact prod” constraint. Please ensure the runbook mentions that aborts are expected and not treated as anomalies by default. Keiko Yamamoto: Added a note under “Interpreting aborts” and linked to the anomaly triage follow-up.
merge_outcome: Merged to main (squash). Follow-up task created to wire abort markers into anomaly triage and rerun policy.
